What the official sources say

  • For damage or other obligation against the deposit, the landlord must mail an itemized notice of damages within 30 days after termination of occupancy, with a check or money order for the difference (or electronic transfer within 10 days after mailing). (MCL 554.609(1)-(3); source)
  • The tenant must respond by mail within 7 days after receipt of the notice of damages or forfeits the amount claimed. (MCL 554.609(4); source)
  • An estate at will may be terminated by 1 month's notice; where rent is payable at periods under 3 months, notice equal to the rent interval is sufficient. (MCL 554.134(1); source)
  • Landlord covenants premises and common areas are fit for intended use and in reasonable repair, and complies with health and safety laws, unless disrepair caused by the tenant's wilful or irresponsible conduct; parties may modify only if the lease term is at least 1 year. (MCL 554.139(1)-(2); source)

Which Michigan landlord tenant rules matter when you sell a rental?

Four sets of rules touch a sale: the security deposit act, the covenants of fitness and repair, the notice rules that end a tenancy, and the summary proceedings that remove an occupant who will not leave. The deposit act is the one a seller cannot skip, because it keeps the old owner on the hook after the closing until the money is handled.

The Landlord-Tenant Act (1972 PA 348) says that when a landlord's interest ends by sale, assignment, death or otherwise, the landlord remains liable for the deposit until it is transferred to the successor with written notice to the tenant by ordinary mail, the successor posts the required bond, or the deposit is returned (MCL 554.614). A seller who closes without moving the deposit and notifying the tenant can still be sued for it.

  • Hand the deposit to the buyer, or return it, before or at closing.
  • Mail the tenant the buyer's name and address in writing.
  • Give the buyer the signed lease, the move-in checklist and the payment ledger.

How much security deposit can a Michigan landlord hold?

The ceiling is one and one-half months' rent (MCL 554.602). A landlord may demand a deposit only if the tenant is told in writing, within 14 days of taking possession, the landlord's name and address for notices, the name and address of the bank or surety holding the funds, and the duty to give a forwarding address within 4 days after moving out (MCL 554.603).

The money must sit in a regulated financial institution. A landlord may use it for other purposes only with a cash or surety bond filed with the secretary of state, covering deposits up to $50,000 and 25 percent of any excess (MCL 554.604). Until the landlord proves a right to it, the deposit is treated as the tenant's property (MCL 554.605).

Deductions are limited to actual damage beyond normal use, unpaid rent, rent due for early termination and unpaid utility bills (MCL 554.607). The landlord also has to use move-in and move-out inventory checklists (MCL 554.608). Buyers inheriting a tenant should ask for both, since a missing move-in checklist weakens any later damage claim.

What are the deadlines for returning a Michigan security deposit?

Within 30 days after the tenant moves out, the landlord must mail an itemized notice of damages with repair estimates, along with a check or money order for any balance. A September 2026 amendment now allows the balance to go by direct deposit or electronic transfer instead, within 10 days after the notice is mailed (MCL 554.609). If the landlord misses the 30 days, the law treats that as agreement that no damages are due, and the full deposit goes back right away (MCL 554.610).

The tenant answers by mail within 7 days. If the tenant never responds, or never gave a forwarding address, the landlord can generally keep the claimed amount. Where there is a real dispute, the landlord has 45 days after move-out to sue for a money judgment or return the balance. Failing to follow the section fully waives the damage claim and makes the landlord liable for double the deposit retained (MCL 554.613).

  • Day 4 after move-out: tenant's written forwarding address due.
  • Day 30: landlord's itemized notice of damages due.
  • Day 7 after receipt: tenant's mailed response due.
  • Day 45: last day for the landlord to file suit over a disputed amount.

What notice ends a Michigan tenancy?

It depends on the tenancy and the reason. An estate at will can be ended by either side with one month's notice, or a notice equal to the rent interval when rent is paid more often than every three months. A year-to-year tenancy ends one year after a notice to quit is served. A landlord can end any tenancy for unpaid rent with a written 7-day notice to quit (MCL 554.134).

A landlord can file for possession in a summary proceeding when a tenant holds over 7 days after a written demand for unpaid rent, and accelerated rent does not count as rent due for that purpose. Shorter periods apply to narrow cases: 24 hours for certain controlled-substance lease terminations after a police report, and 7 days after a notice to quit when a tenant or household member caused or threatened physical injury on the landlord's property (MCL 600.5714).

The same statute lets a person recover possession from someone who stays on after a mortgage or execution sale redemption period ends, or after a personal representative sells under court license or will authority. For an inherited rental, that matters: the buyer from an estate can use summary proceedings against a holdover.

What repair and lease-term rules follow the property to a new owner?

Every residential lease carries a covenant that the premises and common areas are fit for the use intended and kept in reasonable repair, with compliance with state and local health and safety laws. The exception is damage caused by the tenant's willful or irresponsible conduct. Parties can modify the covenant only when the lease term is at least one year (MCL 554.139). A buyer who plans to keep the tenant should walk the unit against that standard before pricing.

The Truth in Renting Act voids lease clauses that waive fitness remedies, waive deposit rights, allow confession of judgment, or let the lessor change terms mid-lease without written consent, with limited 30-day exceptions for tax and utility cost increases (MCL 554.633). If the lease you inherit contains such a clause, it will not hold up, and the buyer should not count on it.

Since April 2025, landlords with five or more rental units may not deny or end a tenancy because of a tenant's source of income, including vouchers and benefits. A tenant who proves a violation can recover actual damages or up to three times the monthly rent, whichever is less, plus costs and attorney fees (MCL 554.601c and 554.601d).

How long does it take to remove an occupant after a judgment?

For an ordinary eviction, the court cannot issue a writ of restitution until 10 days after the judgment for possession, with faster issuance in a few situations the court finds proven, such as forcible entry, trespass or a serious ongoing health hazard (MCL 600.5744). A tenant can stop the writ by paying the judgment amount and costs within the time allowed. If an appeal or new-trial motion is filed with a bond to stay proceedings, the waiting period is paused.

Officers carrying out a writ remove occupants and belongings and either leave the belongings in a public area or deliver them to the sheriff, so the removal itself is done by the court's officer.

More questions about Michigan Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights

What happens to a tenant's security deposit when a Michigan landlord sells the house?

It must follow the property or go back to the tenant. The seller stays liable under MCL 554.614 until the deposit is transferred to the new owner with written notice to the tenant by ordinary mail, the new owner meets the bond requirement, or the deposit is returned.

How much notice does a Michigan landlord give to end a month-to-month tenancy?

One month, or a period equal to the rent interval if rent is paid at intervals shorter than three months. For nonpayment of rent the landlord may instead give a written 7-day notice to quit under MCL 554.134.

How long does a Michigan landlord have to return a deposit?

Thirty days after the tenant moves out to mail an itemized notice of damages and the balance. Missing that deadline means the full deposit must be returned, and an improper withholding can cost the landlord double the amount kept.

Can a Michigan landlord lock out a tenant after an unpaid rent notice?

No. Possession is recovered through summary proceedings, and a court officer carries out the writ of restitution. In the ordinary case the writ cannot issue until 10 days after the judgment for possession.

Do all Michigan landlords have to accept housing vouchers?

Landlords with five or more rental units in the state may not deny or end a tenancy based on source of income, including vouchers, since the 2025 amendment took effect. Owners of fewer than five units are outside that section.

Michigan law requires a landlord to give a specific written notice before filing an eviction, and the number of days depends on the reason.

What the official sources say

  • Nonpayment: landlord may terminate by written 7-day notice to quit. (MCL 554.134(2); source)
  • Summary proceedings for nonpayment when tenant holds over 7 days after service of written demand for possession. (MCL 600.5714(1)(a); source)
  • Serious continuing health hazard or extensive physical damage: 7 days after demand to deliver up possession or substantially restore/repair. (MCL 600.5714(1)(d); source)
  • Controlled substance clause termination: 24-hour notice to quit (with formal police report); violence/threat of injury: 7-day notice to quit. (MCL 554.134(4); 600.5714(1)(b),(e); source)
  • Holdover after lease termination under a lease power, expiration of term, or notice to quit under MCL 554.134 supports summary proceedings; year-to-year tenancy terminated by notice to quit giving 1 year. (MCL 600.5714(1)(c); 554.134(3); source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

When property tax goes unpaid in Michigan, the statutes allow the taxing authority to sell a lien or the property itself, and they give the owner a set time to redeem.

What the official sources say

  • Michigan uses forfeiture and foreclosure: on March 1, property delinquent for the preceding 12 months or more is forfeited to the county treasurer. (MCL 211.78g(1); source)
  • A $175 fee is added to each forfeited property. (MCL 211.78g(1); source)
  • Redemption is allowed until the March 31 after entry of the foreclosure judgment (or 21 days after judgment in a contested case) by paying taxes, interest, penalties, fees. (MCL 211.78g(3); source)
  • Additional interest of 1/2% per month (noncompounded) on originally delinquent taxes, from the preceding March 1, applies on redemption. (MCL 211.78g(3)(b); source)
  • Absolute title and equity vest in the foreclosing governmental unit on the March 31 after judgment; persons with an interest may claim remaining proceeds after sale under section 78t. (MCL 211.78g(2); 2020 PA 256 note; source)
